incident-bot: PAGE: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (eu-west) — SLO breached 03:12 UTC. Automated alerts triggered customers >1min streaming stalls. Auto-escalate to on-call. :rotating_light:

pagerduty: pager duty alert routed to alex_g (on-call) — please acknowledge.

alex_g: ack. I'm on it, pulling up dashboards. seeing p95 ~ 420ms, p99 ~ 2.3s for streaming tokens. Losing steady token emission, stalls every ~6–12s.

maria_s: same on observability — token emission saw many stalled io_wait entries on the runtime host pool. Latency correlates with recent precision-profile rollout: "int8-fastpath-v3" pushed ~02:45 UTC to eu-west.

jon_runtime: adding context: int8-fastpath-v3 enabled a new quantized matmul path with aggressive pack/unpack optimizations for small-batch streaming. We took a narrow canary but it looks like tail behavior degrades for long-context sessions.

liam_sre: customer impact — our CS logs show three paying customers (acct A, B, C) experienced repeated stream stalls and at least one 504 timeout. Working to quantify dropped tokens.

rebecca_pm: any sign of fallback happening? We should check routing to compatible variants.

alex_g: running a quick query: `select count(*) from stream_events where event='stall' and region='eu-west' and ts > now() - interval '1 hour'` — results jumping.

alex_g: pro tip — we'll try traffic-split rollback to int8-fastpath-v2 and enable short-term FP fallback for long-context requests. Taking manual control of variant routing now.

jon_runtime: here's the plan I'm starting:
1) disable int8-fastpath-v3 routing for /v1/stream in eu-west (canary pool)
2) force fallback to fp16-preserve for active long-context sessions
3) enable additional concurrency headroom on runtime pool to reduce queuing

maria_s: logs snippet from worker-03 at 03:13:45: ```
[03:13:45.312] WARN streaming_emit: token_delay=620ms kv_cache_miss=0.83 dequant_ns=120000
[03:13:45.313] DEBUG matmul: input_chunks=5 path=int8_fastpack latency_ns=1300000
[03:13:45.314] ERROR stall_detector: stall_count=3 session_id=xyz123
```

jon_runtime: looks like dequant_ns + int8 path overhead accumulates under certain attention patterns — likely small-batch attention fragmentation.

liam_sre: actioned rollback of routing at 03:19 UTC — traffic now split 95% -> int8-fastpath-v2, 5% -> int8-fastpath-v3 for telemetry. Noting a drop in p99 already on dashboards.

alex_g: I'm patching a temporary request classifier to detect long-context streaming (>2048 tokens) and pin them to fp16-preserve. Deploying a hotfix rule via routes-control: `routes-control set /v1/stream --long-context=fp16-preserve`

maria_s: after rollback + classifier, observed p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 460ms at 03:26 UTC. Streaming stalls markedly reduced but still seeing occasional 1s blips.

rebecca_pm: customer_ops, can we notify affected customers? mention mitigation and ETA for full rollback?

customer_ops: contacting acct A and B now. message: "We've mitigated an intermittent streaming stall in EU region; we routed you to a stable variant and are continuing monitoring. Please contact us if you see anything else."

jon_runtime: root cause hypothesis: int8-fastpath-v3 introduced a packing optimization that reduces per-op throughput for fragmented attention windows (common in multi-turn streaming). On long sessions it causes bursty scheduling and KV cache pressure, which shows as stalls. Fallback to fp16 avoids the new pack/unpack path.

liam_sre: additional mitigations applied: increased worker_ring_size on eu-west runtimes from 256 -> 384, and elevated autoscaler min_replicas by +2 for priority pool. Keeping rollback in place until a stable patch is validated.

alex_g: starting a controlled A/B test to validate a fix from jon_runtime — will monitor for 30m and gradually reintroduce v3 only to short-context traffic.

maria_s: telemetry note: we captured 12 stacktraces where `matmul_fastpack()` waits on `kv_cache_lock` during cross-attention. I'll attach traces to the issue.

rebecca_pm: classification of customer impact: degraded quality of service (stream stalls) — 3 customers impacted, one had request timeouts. No data leakage. We're treating as severity 2 for SLO/routing; ops follow-up required for release gating.

liam_sre: creating incident ticket in tracker: INF-2026-1129, linking telemetry and affected customer list.

alex_g: handing off to night on-call @maria_s at 03:45 UTC. Handoff notes: rollback active, long-context classifier enabled, autoscaler min_replicas bumped, follow-up tasks for runtime/ML infra. Please escalate if p99 > 700ms or customer reports new timeouts.

maria_s: ack handoff. I'll keep monitoring dashboards and will coordinate tomorrow morning with jon_runtime for a proper patch release and QA. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INF-2026-1129 updated: status=mitigated, mitigation=rollback+fp16-fallback, owner=maria_s, next_update=2026-03-15T08:00:00Z.

alex_g: thumbs up. Postmortem and release gating meeting scheduled for 2026-03-15 09:30 UTC (rebecca_pm to lead).

rebecca_pm: added agenda: reproducer, telemetry gaps, release process change (canary criteria for precision profiles), customer comms draft.

customer_ops: all notified; customers reported improved behaviour after the rollback. We'll escalate reopens if anything recurs. :sos:

jon_runtime: follow-ups for tomorrow: produce minimal test harness for long-context streaming under int8-fastpack, add KV cache contention metrics to runtime, and add auto-fallback policy when token emission stalls >3x in 30s.

liam_sre: closing note: good triage and rollback speed. Keep the canary windows stricter for precision profile rollouts.

alex_g: closing thread for now — monitoring continues.
